summary: Finalized the concrete component structure and data flow for Resource Cost's real schema, building on solution-architect's round-2 SDD (tasks/agent-outputs/solution-architect/FEAT-5.json) and architecture-critic's PASS. Authored and applied backend/migrations/0013_add_resource_cost_columns.sql live via mcp__Supabase__apply_migration (per this task's instruction that a schema change isn't real/testable until applied, and per the SDD's own note assigning migration authorship to this stage). Confirmed resource_cost held 0 rows before altering it, so the plain (no sentinel-default) column-add form was used and `name` was dropped outright in the same migration, no two-phase deprecation needed. Live schema verified by direct SELECT against information_schema.columns after apply: id/created_at/updated_at/deleted_at/created_by/updated_by (unchanged) plus employee_id (integer, not null), offshore_cost (numeric, nullable), onsite_cost (numeric, nullable) — name column gone. Adopted architecture-critic's Advisory #1: the FK constraint is named fk_resource_cost_resources (database.md's fk_<table>_<ref_table> convention), not the SDD draft's resource_cost_employee_id_fkey.

migration_applied.pre_migration_check: select count(*) from resource_cost -> 0 rows, confirmed directly before writing the migration form (not taken on a prior stage's word, per subagent-verification discipline even though no subagent was involved here).
statements: add column employee_id integer not null (no sentinel default — table was empty)
add column offshore_cost numeric (nullable, no default)
add column onsite_cost numeric (nullable, no default)
add constraint fk_resource_cost_resources foreign key (employee_id) references public.resources (employee_id)
migration_applied.rls_and_triggers_untouched: resource_cost's RLS-enabled-no-policies state and trg_resource_cost_updated_at trigger (both from migration 0011) are unmodified — 0013 is pure ADD/DROP COLUMN + constraint/index, matching 0012's precedent.
migration_applied.post_apply_verification: Read back information_schema.columns for resource_cost directly after apply_migration returned success — employee_id/offshore_cost/onsite_cost present with correct types/nullability, name absent.

component_structure_for_stage_3.5_4.principle: Three opt-in extensions to the existing generic master-data machine (backend/src/masterDataTables.js descriptor shape, masterDataSchema.js, masterDataRouter.js), each gated so the other 8 tables' current code path is provably unchanged — no bespoke resource_cost route/controller file. This is what stage 3.5 (Engineer MVP) builds and stage 4 (Developer) completes.

1_masterDataTables.js_change.what: resource_cost's entry replaces its single `{ key: 'name', ... }` field with the three real fields, and gains two new table-level descriptor keys.
1_masterDataTables.js_change.other_tables: practices/delivery_centers/competencies/modules/resources/departments/teams/resource_deployment entries are untouched — sortColumn/lookups absent on all of them, so masterDataRouter.js's fallback branches (`table.sortColumn ?? 'name'`, `if (table.lookups)`) take the old code path for every one of them.

validateReferences.signature: export async function validateReferences(table, body, { partial = false } = {})
validateReferences.placement: new function alongside the existing synchronous validateBody, called from masterDataRouter.js's POST/PATCH handlers immediately after validateBody() succeeds (so a plain type/required failure is reported before an extra DB round-trip for the FK check)
validateReferences.logic: for each field with a `validateExists` descriptor, using validateBody's own present/mustValidate semantics (required-on-create, present-on-update): `select 1 from ${ref.table} where ${ref.column} = $1 and deleted_at is null limit 1`; zero rows -> throw validationError({ [field.key]: '<key> must reference an existing, non-deleted <ref.table> row.' })
validateReferences.identifier_safety: ref.table/ref.column come only from the fixed MASTER_DATA_TABLES descriptor (never request input) — same interpolation-safety argument masterDataRouter.js's header comment already makes for tableName/column.

2_masterDataSchema.js_changes.toResponse_change: after the existing per-field loop, `if (table.lookups) { for (const [responseKey, sourceCol] of Object.entries(table.lookups.select)) { response[responseKey] = row[toSnakeAlias(sourceCol)]; } }` — reads off the joined/aliased columns the new SELECT produces (see below), never off table.fields, since employeeName/employeeDesignation must never be writable.

3_masterDataRouter.js_changes.GET_list_and_GET_one_query: when `table.lookups` is set, build `select t.*, j.name as employee_name, j.designation as employee_designation from ${tableName} t left join ${lookups.table} j on j.${lookups.on} = t.${lookups.on} and j.deleted_at is null where ...` instead of `select * from ${tableName}` — LEFT JOIN so a resource_cost row whose employee no longer resolves (soft-deleted or removed) still lists, with employeeName/employeeDesignation coming back null rather than the row vanishing. The select-list of joined columns is generated from `lookups.select`'s values, not hand-written per table, so a future table (e.g. resource_deployment) can reuse this by adding its own `lookups` descriptor with zero router changes.
3_masterDataRouter.js_changes.ORDER_BY_change: `order by (deleted_at is not null), name asc` -> `order by (deleted_at is not null), ${table.sortColumn ?? 'name'} asc`. resource_cost sets sortColumn: 'employee_id' (required, always present post-migration, unlike the independently-nullable cost fields) so the list query is valid against the post-migration schema (no `name` column left to sort by). Every other table keeps sorting by `name` via the fallback.
3_masterDataRouter.js_changes.POST_and_PATCH_change: call `await validateReferences(table, req.body, { partial: <true on PATCH> })` immediately after the existing `validateBody(...)` call, before the INSERT/UPDATE statement runs — so a bad employeeId is rejected as a 422 before it ever reaches Postgres (never surfaces as a raw FK-violation 500). The DB-level `fk_resource_cost_resources` constraint (already live) is defense-in-depth only, per database.md and tech-lead's direction; it should never actually fire against this endpoint once validateReferences is wired in correctly.
3_masterDataRouter.js_changes.employeeName/employeeDesignation_not_wri: since these two keys are never added to resource_cost's `fields[]`, the existing column-building logic in POST/PATCH (`fields.map(f => f.column)` / `fields.map(f => req.body[f.key])`) never references them — a request body containing employeeName is silently ignored, identical to today's handling of any other unknown key. No new code needed for this; it falls out of the existing field-driven column list.

4_mcp_server_mirror.change: resource_cost's fields[] mirrors the backend's employeeId/offshoreCost/onsiteCost shape (numbers), dropping the old `name` field. add_resource_cost/update_resource_cost need no new code — mcp-server/src/index.js already builds each tool's zod shape generically off fields[] (z.number() for type:'number'), and the FK-must-exist requirement is enforced once, in the backend, and simply propagates back through the existing HTTP-error-to-tool-error path (per tech-lead's 'MCP layer stays thin, validate once' direction). Tool descriptions should state the FK-must-exist requirement in the employeeId field's label text, contrasting explicitly with modules.practiceId's 'not validated' language, so an MCP caller isn't surprised by the 422.
4_mcp_server_mirror.no_bespoke_validation_on_mcp_side: confirmed via reading mcp-server/src/masterDataTables.js's structure (mirrors backend descriptors, forwards to backend HTTP API via apiClient.js) — adding a second employeeId-exists check there would create exactly the two-mirrors-drift risk enterprise-architect-pre and tech-lead both flagged; not done.

5_frontend_change.change: resource_cost's columns[] becomes employeeId ("Employee ID") / employeeName ("Employee Name") / employeeDesignation ("Employee Designation") / offshoreCost ("Offshore Cost") / onsiteCost ("Onsite Cost"), then ...AUDIT_COLUMNS unchanged — matches FEAT-6's Employee-<Field> convention. Display-only; dashboard stays read-only, so no form/pick-list component is built (writes go through the MCP server only, per this task's scope).

data_flow_summary.read_path: Client -> GET /v1/resource-cost[/:id] -> masterDataRouter (lookups-aware SELECT with LEFT JOIN resources) -> toResponse (fields[] columns + lookups.select projections) -> { data }
data_flow_summary.write_path: MCP tool call (add_resource_cost/update_resource_cost, employeeId as z.number()) -> apiClient.js -> POST/PATCH /v1/resource-cost[/:id] (requireInternalApiKey) -> validateBody (type/required) -> validateReferences (employeeId exists in resources, not soft-deleted) -> INSERT/UPDATE (fields[] columns only, FK constraint as DB-level backstop) -> toResponse (re-fetch not required; INSERT/UPDATE ... returning * lacks the joined columns, so the write-path response omits employeeName/employeeDesignation unless the router re-queries with the join after insert/update — flagged below as an implementation nuance for stage 3.5).

caching_strategy: None needed — matches every other master-data table (no caching layer exists anywhere in this codebase; resource_cost's read volume/shape gives no reason to introduce one here).
implementation_nuance_flagged_for_stage_: POST/PATCH currently build their response directly from the `insert/update ... returning *` row, which won't carry the joined employee_name/employee_designation aliases (those only exist in the lookups-aware SELECT). Stage 3.5/4 should either (a) have toResponse tolerate missing lookup columns by falling back to null when table.lookups is set but the row wasn't joined, or (b) have POST/PATCH re-run the lookups-aware SELECT for the affected id before responding, for consistency with GET. Recommend (a) for POST (the caller already knows what it sent) and either is acceptable for PATCH; this is an implementation detail within the SDD's design, not a new architectural decision, so it does not require another architecture-critic round.
